headline: Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger dominates UK and North American media
date_line: Saturday 08 August 2026 · covering Thu 06 Aug to Fri 07 Aug

digest.headline: Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger dominates UK and North American media
digest.lead: The UK government has cleared the Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery merger following guarantees for Channel 5. Meanwhile, a US federal court has scheduled a 2027 trial for lawsuits seeking to block the same proposed deal as the FCC repeals national television station ownership caps.

glance.text: Eighteen media organisations have urged the government to reject plans for BBC podcast advertising, warning of risks to the sector.
ITV reported solid first-half results, maintaining its full-year guidance despite a twenty million pound hit from new food advertising regulations.
The BBC has hired twenty-six-year-old entrepreneur Brandon Relph to help the broadcaster reach younger audiences.
The BBC has secured the UK broadcast rights to stream the ATHLOS London all-women's professional track and field event live in September.
Nielsen has agreed to acquire digital measurement firm DoubleVerify and take it private in a deal valued at 2.15 billion dollars.
A federal court has scheduled a 2027 trial for lawsuits seeking to block the proposed merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery.
OpenAI is reportedly developing an artificial intelligence smart speaker priced between 300 and 400 dollars that features moving parts.
Bell Media posted a revenue boost in the second quarter, driven by its streaming service Crave and the FIFA World Cup.
A federal judge ruled that Nexstar officials cannot serve on the board of Tegna while an order to separate them remains.

paragraphs: The UK Competition and Markets Authority has cleared Paramount Skydance's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery [15]. Culture secretary Lisa Nandy confirmed she will not intervene in the eighty-five billion pound deal [16].
The decision follows guarantees secured by the government regarding the future of Channel 5 [16].

A coalition of eighteen media businesses has written to the Culture Secretary to oppose plans for BBC podcast advertising [11, 35]. The group, which includes broadcasters, audio producers, and news publishers, warned the proposals pose serious risks to the wider audio industry [2].

ITV has reported solid first-half financial results in its first update since announcing its deal with Sky [3]. The broadcaster maintained its full-year guidance, aided by an advertising boost from the FIFA Men's World Cup [3].
However, new regulations on less healthy foods reduced its revenue by twenty million pounds [3].

The BBC has partnered with ATHLOS to become the official UK broadcast partner for the league's first international event in London [5]. The public broadcaster will stream the all-women's professional track and field event live from StoneX Stadium [5].

To combat declining youth engagement, the BBC has hired twenty-six-year-old entrepreneur Brandon Relph for its strategy team [4]. Relph will help the broadcaster compete with content creators on platforms like YouTube and TikTok [4].

The Federal Communications Commission voted two to one to repeal the rule limiting broadcasters from owning stations reaching over 39 percent of US households [17]. The agency will now assess future deals individually using a public interest standard rather than a fixed percentage cap [18]. Critics worry this shift could negatively impact smaller, local television markets [18].

Meanwhile, a federal judge has ruled that Nexstar executives are barred from joining the board of Tegna [13]. The ruling maintains an existing order to keep the two broadcasting companies separate [13]. Separately, the UK government has approved Paramount's proposed takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery [31, 52]. However, David Ellison believes disputes over CNN are delaying the merger, with US court dates now set for 2027 [8].
